outcomes.text: Explain the difference between book-keeping and accounting.
State why a business measures profit and loss.
Explain how accounting information helps monitor progress and make decisions.
Explain assets, liabilities and owner's equity.
Explain and apply the accounting equation.

topics.title: 2.1 The double entry system of book-keeping

outcomes.text: Outline the double entry system.
Process accounting data using double entry.
Prepare ledger accounts and post transactions to them.
Balance ledger accounts and transfer balances to financial statements.
Interpret ledger accounts and their balances.
Recognise the sales ledger, purchases ledger and nominal ledger.
Recognise the invoice, debit note, credit note, statement of account, cheque and receipt.
Complete pro-forma business documents.
Use documents as sources of information, including counterfoils, paying-in slips and bank statements.
Explain the advantage of using various books of prime entry.
Process data in the cash book, petty cash book and the journals (sales, purchases, returns, general).
Post ledger entries from the books of prime entry.

subtopics.title: Discounts, cash book and petty cash

outcomes.text: Distinguish and account for trade discount and cash discount.
Explain the cash book's dual function as book of prime entry and ledger account.
Record bank transfers and other electronic payments and receipts.
Explain and apply the imprest system of petty cash.
Explain that a trial balance lists ledger balances on one date.
Outline the uses and limitations of a trial balance.
Prepare a trial balance from balances and amend one with errors.
Identify errors that do not affect the trial balance: commission, compensating, complete reversal, omission, original entry and principle.
Correct errors with journal entries.
Explain a suspense account as a temporary balancing measure.
Correct errors using suspense accounts.
Adjust profit or loss after correcting errors.
Explain the effect of corrections on the statement of financial position.
Explain the use and purpose of a bank statement.
Update the cash book for charges, interest, errors, credit transfers, direct debits, dividends and standing orders.
Explain the purpose of a bank reconciliation statement.
Prepare one including bank errors, uncredited deposits and unpresented cheques.
Explain the purposes of purchases and sales ledger control accounts.
Identify the books of prime entry that feed control account entries.
Prepare control accounts with credit transactions, receipts, payments, discounts, returns, irrecoverable debts, dishonoured cheques, interest, contras, refunds and opening and closing balances.

topics.title: 4.1 Capital and revenue expenditure and receipts

outcomes.text: Distinguish and account for capital and revenue expenditure.
Distinguish and account for capital and revenue receipts.
Calculate and comment on the effect on profit of incorrect treatment.
Calculate and comment on the effect on asset valuations of incorrect treatment.

topics.title: 4.2 Accounting for depreciation and disposal of non-current assets

outcomes.text: Define depreciation.
Explain why depreciation is accounted for.
Describe the straight-line, reducing balance and revaluation methods.
Prepare ledger accounts and journal entries for the provision of depreciation.
Prepare ledger accounts and journal entries for selling non-current assets using disposal accounts.
Recognise the importance of matching costs and revenues.
Record accrued and prepaid expenses in ledgers and journals.
Record accrued and prepaid incomes in ledgers and journals.

topics.title: 4.4 Irrecoverable debts and provision for doubtful debts

outcomes.text: Explain irrecoverable debts and recovery of debts written off.
Record irrecoverable debts in ledgers and journals.
Record recovery of debts written off.
Explain why a provision for doubtful debts is kept.
Record the creation of and adjustments to the provision.
Explain valuing inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
Prepare simple inventory valuation statements.
Explain the effect of incorrect inventory valuation on gross profit, profit, equity and assets.
Explain advantages and disadvantages of operating as a sole trader.
Explain why income statements and statements of financial position are prepared.
Distinguish a trading business from a service business.
Prepare income statements for trading and service businesses.
Explain that a statement of financial position records assets and liabilities on a date.
Define its content: non-current, intangible and current assets, current and non-current liabilities, capital.
Explain how items in the statement relate to each other.
Prepare statements of financial position for trading and service businesses.
Adjust for depreciation using straight line, reducing balance and revaluation.
Adjust for accrued and prepaid expenses and income.
Adjust for irrecoverable debts and provisions for doubtful debts.
Adjust for goods taken by the owner.
Explain advantages and disadvantages of a partnership.
Outline the importance and contents of a partnership agreement.
Explain the purpose of an appropriation account.
Prepare income statements, appropriation accounts and statements of financial position.
Record interest on loans, capital and drawings, salaries and division of profit or loss.
Make the year-end adjustments from 5.1.
Explain the uses of and differences between capital and current accounts.
Draw up partners' capital and current accounts as ledgers and in the statement of financial position.
Explain advantages and disadvantages of operating as a limited company.
Explain limited liability and equity.
Explain the capital structure: preference shares, ordinary shares, general reserve and retained earnings.
Distinguish issued, called-up and paid-up share capital.
Distinguish share capital from loan capital (debentures).
Prepare income statements, statements of changes in equity and statements of financial position.
Make the year-end adjustments from 5.1.
Distinguish receipts and payments accounts from income and expenditure accounts.
Prepare receipts and payments accounts.
Prepare accounts for revenue-generating activities such as refreshments and subscriptions.
Prepare income and expenditure accounts and statements of financial position.
Make the year-end adjustments from 5.1.
Define and calculate the accumulated fund.
Distinguish direct and indirect costs.
Explain direct material, direct labour, prime cost and factory overheads.
Explain and adjust for work in progress.
Calculate factory cost of production.
Prepare manufacturing accounts, income statements and statements of financial position.
Make the year-end adjustments from 5.1.
Explain the disadvantages of incomplete records.
Prepare opening and closing statements of affairs.
Calculate profit or loss from changes in capital.
Calculate sales, purchases, gross profit, receivables, payables and other figures from incomplete information.
Apply mark-up, margin and inventory turnover to find missing figures.
Prepare income statements and statements of financial position from incomplete records, with the 5.1 adjustments.

topics.title: 6.1 Calculation and understanding of accounting ratios

outcomes.text: Calculate and explain gross margin.
Calculate and explain profit margin.
Calculate and explain return on capital employed (ROCE).
Calculate and explain the current ratio.
Calculate and explain the liquid (acid test) ratio.
Calculate and explain rate of inventory turnover.
Calculate and explain trade receivables and trade payables turnover in days.
Prepare and comment on comparisons of results for different years.
Recommend ways to improve profitability and working capital.
Explain the significance of the gap between gross margin and profit margin.
Explain how gross profit and profit relate to inventory valuation, turnover, revenue, expenses and equity.
Explain the problems of inter-firm comparison.
Apply ratios to compare firms.
Explain how owners and managers use accounting information.
Explain how trade payables, banks and investors use it.
Explain how club members, governments and tax authorities use it.
Recognise limitations from historic cost, difficulties of definition and non-financial aspects.
Explain and recognise matching, business entity, consistency, duality and going concern.
Explain and recognise historic cost, materiality, money measurement, prudence and realisation.
Recognise the influence of international accounting standards.
Explain the policy objectives: comparability, relevance, reliability and understandability.
